## MapReduce {#sec-mapreduce-documentation}


### `MapReduce(UF, UF)`
Creates a `MapReduce` instance with the supplied user functions. The first user function will be used during the `Map` phase, and the second user function will be used during the `Reduce` phase.

```cpp
#include <skepu>

int mult(int a, int b)
{
    return a * b;
}

int sum(int a, int b)
{
    return a + b;
}

int main()
{
    auto dotproduct = skepu::MapReduce(mult, sum);
}
```

### `operator()`
Calls the `MapReduce` instance, performing a `Map` operation on the inputs using the first user function, then a `Reduce` operation on the intermediate result using the second user function, and returns a scalar similar to the `Reduce` skeleton. 

```{.cpp .run}
#include <skepu>
#include <skepu-lib/io.hpp>

int mult(int a, int b)
{
    return a * b;
}

int sum(int a, int b)
{
    return a + b;
}

int main()
{
    skepu::Vector<int> a{1, 2, 3, 4}, b{4, 3, 2, 1};

    auto dotproduct = skepu::MapReduce(mult, sum);
    int result = dotproduct(a, b);
    skepu::io::cout << result << "\n";
}
```

```{.text .output}
20
```

### `setStride(int...)`
Sets the stride of the input containers of the `MapReduce` instance. These strides are used during the `Map` phase of the skeleton. All strides are set to 1 by default.

```{.cpp .run}
#include <skepu>

int mult(int a, int b)
{
    return a * b;
}

int sum(int a, int b)
{
    return a + b;
}

int main()
{
    skepu::Vector<int> a{1, 2, 3, 4}, b{2, 2};

    auto dotproduct = skepu::MapReduce(mult, sum);
    dotproduct.setStride(2, 1);
    std::cout << dotproduct(a, b) << "\n";
}
```

```{.text .output}
8
```
